proofs.proof_tex:
The construction gives \(p_{a,s}(x)=1/6\) for every \(a\in\{2,3,\infty\}\), \(s\in\{0,1\}\), and \(x\in\{-1,1\}\), and therefore \(\pi_{2,1}=1/6\). Since \(|(U^{\mathrm w}+V^{\mathrm w})/8|\le1/4\) and \(|\delta|<1/8\),
\[
\max_{t\in\mathcal T}|Y_t|
\le \frac14+|\delta|<\frac38.
\tag{Q1}
\]
Consistency holds by the last clause of Definition \(\ref{def:binary-witness}\). If \(s=0\), the treatment term is zero at every date, proving no effect on ineligible units. If \(u<a\), then both \(Y_u(a,1)\) and \(Y_u(\infty,1)\) equal \(Z_u^{\mathrm w}\), proving no anticipation. Conditional on \((G,X)\), the distribution of \((U^{\mathrm w},V^{\mathrm w})\) does not depend on \(S\). Hence the untreated eligibility gap within each cohort is zero, and both sides of every global OVS conditional parallel-gap equality are zero. These facts and Definition \(\ref{def:target-model}\) prove \(Q^{\mathrm{bin}}_{r,\delta}\in\mathcal M\).

Moreover, \(r<\sqrt7/3<1\), so every conditional sign probability \(\{1+\rho_a(x)uv\}/4\) is strictly positive. In each observed cohort--eligibility cell, the conditional support of \((\Delta Y_2,\Delta Y_3)\) is therefore all four vertices of a translated square, and its conditional mean is the translated center because both signs have mean zero. That center lies in the relative interior of the convex hull. Thus the induced observed law is a conditional-mean interior law. Equation (Q1) also gives the fourth-moment condition, and \(p_{a,s}=1/6\) gives retained-cell overlap, so the tangent-exhaustion theorem is applicable below.

The signs have conditional means zero. The observed increments are
\[
\Delta Y_2=\frac{U^{\mathrm w}}8
+\delta S\mathbf 1\{G=2\},
\qquad
\Delta Y_3=\frac{V^{\mathrm w}}8
+\delta S\mathbf 1\{G=3\}.
\tag{Q2}
\]
It follows directly from the definition of \(q_{k,c}\) that all three conditional DDD contrasts equal \(\delta\). The two target effects also equal \(\delta\), so \(q_{k,c}(X)-\theta_k(P)=0\) in every score coordinate. Put \(a=3/4\). Because every propensity ratio in Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\) equals one and \(1/\pi_{2,1}=6\), direct substitution gives
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
(G,S)&\Psi_{(2,2),3}&\Psi_{(2,2),\infty}&\Psi_{(2,3),\infty}\\ \hline
(2,1)&aU^{\mathrm w}&aU^{\mathrm w}&a(U^{\mathrm w}+V^{\mathrm w})\\
(2,0)&-aU^{\mathrm w}&-aU^{\mathrm w}&-a(U^{\mathrm w}+V^{\mathrm w})\\
(3,1)&-aU^{\mathrm w}&0&0\\
(3,0)&aU^{\mathrm w}&0&0\\
(\infty,1)&0&-aU^{\mathrm w}&-a(U^{\mathrm w}+V^{\mathrm w})\\
(\infty,0)&0&aU^{\mathrm w}&a(U^{\mathrm w}+V^{\mathrm w}).
\end{array}
\tag{Q3}
\]
Every row has conditional probability \(1/6\), while
\[
E_P[U^{\mathrm w}V^{\mathrm w}\mid X=x,G=2]
=E_P[U^{\mathrm w}V^{\mathrm w}\mid X=x,G=3]=0,
\qquad
E_P[U^{\mathrm w}V^{\mathrm w}\mid X=x,G=\infty]=xr.
\tag{Q4}
\]
The conditional mean of each column of (Q3) is zero. Multiplying the six rows coordinate by coordinate, using \(E[(U^{\mathrm w})^2]=E[(V^{\mathrm w})^2]=1\), gives
\[
\Gamma(x)=\frac{3}{16}
\begin{pmatrix}
2&1&1\\
1&2&2+xr\\
1&2+xr&4+2xr
\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{Q5}
\]
For example, the second--third entry receives one contribution from the cohort-two cells and a contribution \(1+xr\) from the never-treated cells, whereas the third diagonal receives \(2\) and \(2+2xr\), respectively. This verifies every entry in (Q5), including the shared-cell covariances.

Let \(B(x)=16\Gamma(x)/3\). Its first two leading principal minors are \(2\) and \(3\), and direct expansion gives
\[
\det B(x)=6-2x^2r^2=6-2r^2>0,
\tag{Q6}
\]
because \(r^2<7/9<3\). Sylvester's criterion therefore makes \(B(x)\), and hence \(\Gamma(x)\), positive definite. Since \(X\) has only two support points, \(\min_{x\in\{-1,1\}}\lambda_{\min}\{\Gamma(x)\}>0\) at each fixed admissible \(r\).

Feasibility is \(b_1+b_2=\omega_1\) and \(b_3=\omega_2\), so it is equivalent to \(b=b(q)\). With \(d=(1,-1,0)'\), (Q5) gives
\[
\frac{d}{dq}\{b(q)'\Gamma(x)b(q)\}
=2d'\Gamma(x)b(q)
=\frac34\left\{q-\frac{(1+xr)\omega_2}{2}\right\},
\qquad
\frac{d^2}{dq^2}\{b(q)'\Gamma(x)b(q)\}=\frac34>0.
\tag{Q7}
\]
Thus \(q^\star(x)=(1+xr)\omega_2/2\), proving the formula for \(b^\star\) also from the defining conditional quadratic program.

Averaging (Q5) over the symmetric binary \(X\) removes only the terms containing \(xr\). Applying (Q7) to the unconditional objective therefore gives the unique joint-constant minimizer \(q_{\mathrm{const}}=\omega_2/2\). The OVS rule minimizes separately over the first target block, whose unconditional covariance is proportional to
\(\begin{psmallmatrix}2&1\\1&2\end{psmallmatrix}\). Under \(b_1+b_2=\omega_1\), this block has its unique minimizer at \(b_1=b_2=\omega_1/2\), so \(q_{\mathrm{OVS}}=0\); the singleton second block forces \(b_3=\omega_2\). This proves the two comparator formulas.

Taylor's identity is exact for the quadratic in (Q7), and hence for every deterministic \(q\),
\[
E_P\!\left[b(q)'\Gamma(X)b(q)-b\{q^\star(X)\}'\Gamma(X)b\{q^\star(X)\}\right]
=\frac38E_P\!\left[\left\{q-\frac{(1+Xr)\omega_2}{2}\right\}^2\right].
\tag{Q8}
\]
Because \(E_P[X]=0\) and \(E_P[X^2]=1\), the right-hand side is
\[
\frac38\left(q-\frac{\omega_2}{2}\right)^2
+\frac{3r^2\omega_2^2}{32}.
\tag{Q9}
\]

It remains to verify which efficiency frontier (Q9) measures. At period two the published clean set is \(\{3,\infty\}\), giving the single nonzero OVS row \((2,3,\infty)\), while at period three the clean set is the singleton \(\{\infty\}\). The localized construction also has exactly the period-two row: the target \((2,2)\) permits both comparisons, while the target \((2,3)\) permits only \(\infty\). Therefore the deterministic conventions and identical residual formulas imply
\[
Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}=Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}=Z_{2;3,\infty}.
\tag{Q10}
\]
The kernel of \(A'\) is one dimensional, spanned by \((1,-1,0)'\). Subtracting the first two pairwise scores in (Q3), with the target-share correction canceling within the target block, yields
\[
R_{(2,2),3,P}-R_{(2,2),\infty,P}=-Z_{2;3,\infty}.
\tag{Q11}
\]
Thus \(\mathcal C_P\) is precisely the closed measurable span of the single normal in (Q10). The tangent-exhaustion identities in Theorem \(\ref{thm:observable-equivalence}\) show that the same span is both \(\mathcal T_P^\perp\) and \(\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp\). Hence
\[
\mathcal C_P=\mathcal T_P^\perp=\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp,
\qquad
\Delta_{\mathrm{normal}}=\Delta_{\mathrm{model}}=0.
\tag{Q12}
\]
Theorem \(\ref{thm:complete-normal-canonical-gradient}\) and Proposition \(\ref{prop:equality-frontier}\) now identify (Q9) with \(\Delta\{b(q)\}\), the variance loss relative to \(V_{\mathrm{OVS}}\). Substitution of \(q=\omega_2/2\) and \(q=0\) gives the two claimed comparator losses. Finally, at \(r=\omega_2=1/2\), these are respectively \(3/512\) and \(15/512\), and strict convexity in (Q7) proves that the first is the minimum over all deterministic feasible loadings.

The first tangent-normal identity is equation (2) of Theorem \(\ref{thm:observable-equivalence}\). Lemma \(\ref{lem:reference-score-gradient}\) gives, for every \(s\in\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}\),
\[
\dot\tau_{\omega,P}[s]=E_P[\psi_P^0s].
\tag{T1}
\]
Abbreviate \(Z=Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\), \(K=K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\), and \(r=r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\). If \(v\in\ker K(x)\), then
\[
0=v'K(x)v=E_P[(v'Z)^2\mid X=x].
\]
Consequently \(v'Z=0\) conditionally almost surely and \(v'r(x)=E_P[v'Z\psi_P^0\mid X=x]=0\). Symmetry of \(K(x)\) therefore implies
\[
r(x)\in\operatorname{range}K(x),
\qquad
K(x)K(x)^\dagger r(x)=r(x).
\tag{T2}
\]
The Moore--Penrose map is Borel measurable because, for a symmetric matrix,
\[
K^\dagger=\lim_{j\to\infty}(K^2+j^{-1}I)^{-1}K.
\tag{T3}
\]
Put \(p_{\mathrm{OVS},P}=r'K^\dagger Z\). Symmetry and (T2) give
\[
E_P[p_{\mathrm{OVS},P}^2\mid X]
=r'K^\dagger KK^\dagger r
=r'K^\dagger r
=E_P[\psi_P^0p_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\mid X].
\tag{T4}
\]
Conditional Cauchy--Schwarz applied to the last equality shows
\[
0\le E_P[p_{\mathrm{OVS},P}^2\mid X]
\le E_P[(\psi_P^0)^2\mid X],
\]
with the inequality immediate when the left side is zero and obtained by division by its square root otherwise. Since \(\psi_P^0\in L_2(P)\), this proves \(p_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\in L_2(P)\). For every square-integrable measurable multiple \(a(X)'Z\),
\[
E_P[(\psi_P^0-p_{\mathrm{OVS},P})a(X)'Z]
=E_P[a(X)'\{r-KK^\dagger r\}]=0.
\tag{T5}
\]
Equations (T4)--(T5), first for the generating set and then for its \(L_2(P)\)-closure, together with tangent exhaustion prove
\[
p_{\mathrm{OVS},P}=\Pi_{\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp}\psi_P^0,
\qquad
\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}=\Pi_{\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}}\psi_P^0.
\tag{T6}
\]
Combining (T1) and (T6) proves canonicality. Taking expectations in (T4) and expanding \(E_P[(\psi_P^0-p_{\mathrm{OVS},P})^2]\) proves (16). Coefficient versions differing in \(\ker K(X)\) have the same product with \(Z\), so singular or redundant coordinates create no ambiguity in the projected random variable.

The identical calculation with \(Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\), using equation (3) of Theorem \(\ref{thm:observable-equivalence}\), gives
\[
p_{\mathrm{per},P}=\Pi_{\mathcal T_P^\perp}\psi_P^0,
\qquad
\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}=\Pi_{\mathcal T_P}\psi_P^0.
\tag{T7}
\]
Since \(\mathcal T_P^\perp\subseteq\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp\), nested orthogonal projections imply
\[
\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}
=\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}+(p_{\mathrm{OVS},P}-p_{\mathrm{per},P}),
\]
where the two terms on the right are orthogonal. Pythagoras proves (17). Moreover, \(p_{\mathrm{per},P}\) belongs to the published normal space, so \(\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}\) is still a gradient on the published subclass. It is canonical there exactly when it is orthogonal to the closed span of the measurable multiples of \(Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\), equivalently when the conditional moment in (18) is zero.

On the observable equality model, every residual in Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\) has conditional mean zero, and every comparison in a target block has the same conditional contrast. Hence
\[
E_P[\Psi_P\mid X]=Ah(X).
\tag{T8}
\]
Every feasible loading therefore has conditional mean \(\omega'h(X)\). The conditional variance identity yields
\[
\operatorname{Var}_P\{b(X)'\Psi_P\}
=\operatorname{Var}_P\{\omega'h(X)\}
+E_P[b(X)'\Gamma_P(X)b(X)].
\tag{T9}
\]
Lemma \(\ref{lem:singular-operator}\) gives \(A'b^\star=\omega\) and \(N'\Gamma b^\star=0\). If \(d=b-b^\star\), then \(A'd=0\), so \(d=Nz\) for a measurable coefficient \(z\), and \(d'\Gamma b^\star=0\). Expanding the quadratic in (T9) proves (19)--(20), including the singular fixed-rank case.

Let \(b^{\mathrm{ref}}\) put weight \(\omega_k\) on \((k,c_0(k))\) and zero on the other coordinates. Then \(\psi_P^0=b^{\mathrm{ref}\prime}\Psi_P\). Since \(b^{\mathrm{ref}}-b^\star\in\operatorname{col}N\), the target-share correction cancels within every block and
\[
p_{\mathrm{agg},P}:=\psi_P^0-\phi_{\mathrm{agg},P}
=(b^{\mathrm{ref}}-b^\star(X))'R_P\in\mathcal C_P.
\tag{T10}
\]
Using \(N'R=N'\Psi\), (T8), \(N'A=0\), and \(N'\Gamma b^\star=0\),
\[
E_P[N'R_P\phi_{\mathrm{agg},P}\mid X]
=N'\{\Gamma_P+Ahh'A'\}b^\star=0.
\tag{T11}
\]
Thus \(p_{\mathrm{agg},P}=\Pi_{\mathcal C_P}\psi_P^0\). The nested closed normal spaces
\[
\mathcal C_P\subseteq\mathcal T_P^\perp
\subseteq\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp
\]
have orthogonal successive projection increments. Pythagoras proves (21). Finally, orthogonality to all square-integrable measurable multiples of a finite normal vector is equivalent, by iterated expectation, to a zero conditional cross-moment with that vector. Applying this equivalence to \(Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\) and \(Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\) proves the two stated equality characterizations, including (22). This derivation makes \(\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\), rather than \(b^\star(X)'\Psi_P\) absent (22), the canonical gradient of the published model.

If every \(\mathcal J_k\) is a singleton, then \(M=K_0\), and under the fixed target ordering the incidence matrix \(A\) is the identity. Thus \(\ker(A')=\{0\}\), \(N\) has no columns, and \(A'b=\omega\) has one solution. The conditional and constant loading programs consequently coincide. Proposition \(\ref{prop:two-period-eif-reduction}\) supplies the theorem-level, source-transcribed term-by-term reduction of this just-identified score to both the Ortiz--Villavicencio--Sant'Anna and Akbari--Kiyavash--Ghassami two-period panel-DDD efficient influence functions; no resemblance-based identification is used.

If \(X\) is degenerate, then \(\Gamma(X)=\Gamma\) almost surely. Equation (T8) in Theorem \(\ref{thm:complete-normal-canonical-gradient}\) and total covariance give
\[
\Omega=E_P[\Gamma(X)]+\operatorname{Var}_P\{Ah(X)\}=\Gamma,
\]
because \(Ah(X)=E_P[\Psi\mid X]\) is constant and \(E_P[\Psi]=0\). Hence the conditional and constant quadratic programs have the same objective. Write \(b=b^0+Nz\). Since \(b^0\in\operatorname{col}A\) and \(Nz\in\ker A'\), the two terms are Euclidean-orthogonal. Lemma \(\ref{lem:singular-operator}\) selects
\[
z=-H^\dagger N'\Gamma b^0\in\operatorname{range}H,
\]
which is the minimum-Euclidean-norm solution of the normal equations. This is exactly the Moore--Penrose convention defining \(b^{\mathrm{const}}\).

Theorem \(\ref{thm:complete-normal-canonical-gradient}\) proves more generally that a loaded pairwise score is canonical only after its published normal equation is verified. The exact external identification used in the just-identified reduction is isolated in Proposition \(\ref{prop:two-period-eif-reduction}\) and its two cited theorem-level leaves. Thus the theorem makes no unsupported identification with an externally published efficient influence function.

added_lemmas.statement:
In the two-period panel design with enabling cohort \(C\in\{2,\infty\}\), eligibility \(E\in\{0,1\}\), outcome change \(D=Y_2-Y_1\), and covariates \(X\), define \(p_{a,s}(x)=P(C=a,E=s\mid X=x)\), \(\mu_{a,s}(x)=E[D\mid C=a,E=s,X=x]\), and
\[
\tau(X)=D-\mu_{2,0}(X)-\mu_{\infty,1}(X)+\mu_{\infty,0}(X).
\]
Under the source's random-sampling, strong-overlap, no-anticipation, and conditional DDD parallel-trends assumptions, Ortiz--Villavicencio and Sant'Anna's Lemma A.2 states that the efficient influence function for \(\operatorname{ATT}(2,2)\) is
\[
\eta_{\mathrm{OVS}}
=w_{\mathrm{trt}}^{2,1}(C,E)\{\tau(X)-\operatorname{ATT}(2,2)\}
-w_{\mathrm{comp}}^{2,0}(C,E,X)\{D-\mu_{2,0}(X)\}
-w_{\mathrm{comp}}^{\infty,1}(C,E,X)\{D-\mu_{\infty,1}(X)\}
+w_{\mathrm{comp}}^{\infty,0}(C,E,X)\{D-\mu_{\infty,0}(X)\},
\]
where
\[
w_{\mathrm{trt}}^{2,1}(C,E)=\frac{\mathbf 1\{C=2,E=1\}}{E[\mathbf 1\{C=2,E=1\}]},
\qquad
w_{\mathrm{comp}}^{a,s}(C,E,X)
=\frac{\mathbf 1\{C=a,E=s\}p_{2,1}(X)/p_{a,s}(X)}{E[\mathbf 1\{C=a,E=s\}p_{2,1}(X)/p_{a,s}(X)]}.
\]

source.locator: Supplemental Appendix, Lemma A.2, PDF pages 44--45
source.verbatim_statement: Lemma A.2 (Efficient Influence Function). Suppose Assumptions S, SO, NA, and DDD-CPT hold. Let \(\tau(X)=Y_2-Y_1-m^{S=2,Q=0}_{Y_2-Y_1}(X)-m^{S=\infty,Q=1}_{Y_2-Y_1}(X)+m^{S=\infty,Q=0}_{Y_2-Y_1}(X)\). Then \(\eta_{\mathrm{eff}}=w^{S=2,Q=1}_{\mathrm{trt}}\{\tau(X)-\operatorname{ATT}(2,2)\}-w^{S=2,Q=0}_{\mathrm{comp}}\{Y_2-Y_1-m^{S=2,Q=0}_{Y_2-Y_1}(X)\}-w^{S=\infty,Q=1}_{\mathrm{comp}}\{Y_2-Y_1-m^{S=\infty,Q=1}_{Y_2-Y_1}(X)\}+w^{S=\infty,Q=0}_{\mathrm{comp}}\{Y_2-Y_1-m^{S=\infty,Q=0}_{Y_2-Y_1}(X)\}\) is the efficient influence function, where \(w^{S=2,Q=1}_{\mathrm{trt}}=\mathbf 1\{S=2,Q=1\}/E[\mathbf 1\{S=2,Q=1\}]\) and \(w^{S=g,Q=q}_{\mathrm{comp}}=\{\mathbf 1\{S=g,Q=q\}p^{S=2,Q=1}(X)/p^{S=g,Q=q}(X)\}/E[\mathbf 1\{S=g,Q=q\}p^{S=2,Q=1}(X)/p^{S=g,Q=q}(X)]\).

attestation.note: Transcribed from arXiv:2505.09942v3, Supplemental Appendix, Lemma A.2, including the displayed target and comparison weights immediately following the formula.

added_lemmas.statement:
In the two-period panel design of Akbari, Kiyavash, and Ghassami, let \(G_A,D_A\in\{0,1\}\), \(D_Y=Y_1-Y_0\), \(\mu_{a,s,\Delta}(X)=E[D_Y\mid X,G_A=a,D_A=s]\), \(\pi=E[G_AD_A]\),
\[
\psi_{\mathrm{pd}}
=E[\mu_{1,1,\Delta}(X)-\mu_{0,1,\Delta}(X)-\mu_{1,0,\Delta}(X)+\mu_{0,0,\Delta}(X)\mid G_A=1,D_A=1],
\]
\(\pi_{r,a,s}(X)=P(G_A=1,D_A=1\mid X)/P(G_A=a,D_A=s\mid X)\), and
\[
w_{a,s}(X,G_A,D_A)=G_AD_A-\mathbf 1\{G_A=a,D_A=s\}\pi_{r,a,s}(X).
\]
Their Theorem 5 states that, in the nonparametric model, the efficient influence function of the panel DDD target \(\psi_{\mathrm{pd}}\) is
\[
\psi_{\mathrm{pd}}^1(O)
=\frac1\pi\sum_{a,s\in\{0,1\}}(-1)^{a+s+1}
w_{a,s}(X,G_A,D_A)\{D_Y-\mu_{a,s,\Delta}(X)\}
-\frac{G_AD_A}{\pi}\psi_{\mathrm{pd}}.
\]

source.locator: Section 4.1 target definition and Theorem 5, equation (6), PDF pages 8--9
source.verbatim_statement: Section 4.1 defines \(\psi_{\mathrm{pd}}=E[(Y_1-Y_0-\mu_{0,1,\Delta}(X)-\mu_{1,0,\Delta}(X)+\mu_{0,0,\Delta}(X))\mathbf 1\{G=1,D=1\}]/E[\mathbf 1\{G=1,D=1\}]\). Theorem 5 states that its efficient influence function is \(\psi^1_{\mathrm{pd}}(O)=E[G D]^{-1}\sum_{g,d\in\{0,1\}}(-1)^{g+d+1}w_{g,d}(X,G,D)\{Y_1-Y_0-\mu_{g,d,\Delta}(X)\}-G D\psi_{\mathrm{pd}}/E[G D]\), where \(\mu_{g,d,\Delta}(X)=E[Y_1-Y_0\mid X,G=g,D=d]\), \(w_{g,d}=G D-\mathbf 1\{G=g,D=d\}\pi_{r,g,d}(X)\), and \(\pi_{r,g,d}(X)=p(G=1,D=1\mid X)/p(G=g,D=d\mid X)\).

attestation.note: Transcribed from arXiv:2502.19788v3, Section 4.1 and Theorem 5, equation (6), including the displayed panel target and the definitions of the conditional regression and propensity ratio.

added_lemmas.statement:
Chen, Sant'Anna, and Xie's Theorem 3.2 studies staggered DiD observed data \((Y_1,\ldots,Y_T,X,G)\) under their random-sampling, overlap, no-anticipation, and all-period parallel-trends assumptions. If \(\operatorname{IF}^{\operatorname{att}(g,t)}_{\mathrm{stg}}\) stacks their noncollinear DiD influence functions based on the available baseline periods and comparison cohorts and \(\Omega_{gt}(X)\) is its conditional second-moment matrix, their efficient influence function is the normalized conditional precision combination
\[
\operatorname{EIF}^{\operatorname{att}(g,t)}_{\mathrm{stg}}
=\frac{\mathbf 1'\Omega_{gt}(X)^{-1}}{\mathbf 1'\Omega_{gt}(X)^{-1}\mathbf 1}
\operatorname{IF}^{\operatorname{att}(g,t)}_{\mathrm{stg}}.
\]
The theorem's observed vector contains no eligibility variable and its parallel-trends restrictions are DiD restrictions, not the four-cell eligibility-gap equalities used by the present DDD model.

source.verbatim_statement: Theorem 3.2. Suppose that treatment adoption is staggered over time. Under Assumptions S, O, NA and PT-All, \(\operatorname{EIF}^{\operatorname{att}(g,t)}_{\mathrm{stg}}=\{\mathbf 1'\Omega_{gt}(X)^{-1}\}/\{\mathbf 1'\Omega_{gt}(X)^{-1}\mathbf 1\}\operatorname{IF}^{\operatorname{att}(g,t)}_{\mathrm{stg}}\) is the efficient influence function of \(\operatorname{ATT}(g,t)\).

attestation.note: Transcribed from arXiv:2506.17729, Theorem 3.2, together with the observed-data vector and stacked-influence-function definitions in Lemma 3.2 and the paragraphs immediately preceding the theorem.

added_lemmas.statement:
Consider the two-period, two-cohort specialization with a single target \(k=(g,g)\), a single clean comparison \(\mathcal J_k=\{c\}\), the outcome change \(D=\Delta Y_g\), and unit aggregate weight \(\omega_k=1\). Relabel the target cohort and comparison cohort as \(G_A=1\) and \(G_A=0\), respectively, and relabel eligibility \(S\) as \(D_A\). Then the efficient influence functions in Ortiz--Villavicencio and Sant'Anna's Lemma A.2 and Akbari, Kiyavash, and Ghassami's Theorem 5 both reduce, term by term, to the core score \(\Psi_{k,c,P}\). Because the relevant published clean set is a singleton, there is no nonzero published OVS normal row and
\[
\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}=\psi_P^0=\Psi_{k,c,P}.
\]
For a scalar aggregate weight \(\omega_k\), all three expressions are multiplied by \(\omega_k\). Thus the exhaustive staggered-DDD canonical gradient has both published panel-DDD formulas as an exact just-identified special case. This algebraic reduction does not assert that the staggered-DiD conditional-efficiency model of Chen, Sant'Anna, and Xie is nested in, or contains, the eligibility-gap DDD model.
added_lemmas.justification: The proposition supplies the exact sourced just-identified panel-DDD regression test required to compare the exhaustive staggered construction with the nearest published DDD influence functions.
added_lemmas.gap: The equality is a two-period singleton-comparison specialization; it does not identify the distinct staggered-DiD tangent system with the eligibility-gap DDD system.
added_lemmas.consumer: The known-reductions theorem and the optional backend use this identity as a term-by-term score regression test.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every \(0<r<\sqrt 7/3\), \(0<|\delta|<1/8\), and \(\omega=(\omega_1,\omega_2)'\) with \(\omega_2\ne0\), the law \(Q^{\mathrm{bin}}_{r,\delta}\) belongs to \(\mathcal M\), and its outcomes satisfy \(\max_{t\in\mathcal T}|Y_t|<3/8\) almost surely. In score order \(((2,2),3),((2,2),\infty),((2,3),\infty)\),
\[
\Gamma(x)=\frac{3}{16}
\begin{pmatrix}
2&1&1\\
1&2&2+xr\\
1&2+xr&4+2xr
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Its leading principal minors before multiplication by \(3/16\) are \(2\), \(3\), and \(6-2r^2\); hence \(\Gamma(x)\) is positive definite for both \(x\in\{-1,1\}\), and its conditional eigenvalues are separated from zero at every fixed \(r\) in the displayed range. Every feasible loading has the form
\[
b(q)=\bigl(\omega_1/2+q,\ \omega_1/2-q,\ \omega_2\bigr)',
\]
and the conditional optimum is
\[
q^\star(x)=\frac{(1+xr)\omega_2}{2},
\qquad
b^\star(x)=b\{q^\star(x)\}.
\]
The best joint constant and published componentwise loadings are distinct:
\[
b^{\mathrm{const}}=b(\omega_2/2),
\qquad
b^{\mathrm{OVS}}=b(0).
\]
For every deterministic \(q\), the loss relative to the published OVS bound is
\[
\Delta\{b(q)\}
=\frac{3}{8}\left(q-\frac{\omega_2}{2}\right)^2
+\frac{3r^2\omega_2^2}{32}.
\]
Consequently
\[
\Delta(b^{\mathrm{const}})=\frac{3r^2\omega_2^2}{32}>0,

proposed.statement:
For every \(0<r<\sqrt 7/3\), \(0<|\delta|<1/8\), and \(\omega=(\omega_1,\omega_2)'\) with \(\omega_2\ne0\), the law \(Q^{\mathrm{bin}}_{r,\delta}\) belongs to \(\mathcal M\), and its outcomes satisfy \(\max_{t\in\mathcal T}|Y_t|<3/8\) almost surely. In score order \(((2,2),3),((2,2),\infty),((2,3),\infty)\),
\[
\Gamma(x)=\frac{3}{16}
\begin{pmatrix}
2&1&1\\
1&2&2+xr\\
1&2+xr&4+2xr
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Its leading principal minors before multiplication by \(3/16\) are \(2\), \(3\), and \(6-2r^2\); hence \(\Gamma(x)\) is positive definite for both \(x\in\{-1,1\}\), and its conditional eigenvalues are separated from zero at every fixed \(r\) in the displayed range. Every feasible loading has the form
\[
b(q)=\bigl(\omega_1/2+q,\ \omega_1/2-q,\ \omega_2\bigr)',
\]
and the conditional optimum is
\[
q^\star(x)=\frac{(1+xr)\omega_2}{2},
\qquad
b^\star(x)=b\{q^\star(x)\}.
\]
The best joint constant and published componentwise loadings are distinct:
\[
b^{\mathrm{const}}=b(\omega_2/2),
\qquad
b^{\mathrm{OVS}}=b(0).
\]
For every deterministic \(q\), the loss relative to the published OVS bound is
\[
\Delta\{b(q)\}
=\frac{3}{8}\left(q-\frac{\omega_2}{2}\right)^2
+\frac{3r^2\omega_2^2}{32}.
\]
Consequently
\[
\Delta(b^{\mathrm{const}})=\frac{3r^2\omega_2^2}{32}>0,
\qquad
\Delta(b^{\mathrm{OVS}})=\frac{3(1+r^2)\omega_2^2}{32}>0.
\]
In this architecture the deterministic row conventions give
\[
Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}=Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}=Z_{2;3,\infty},
\qquad
\mathcal C_P=\mathcal T_P^\perp=\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp.
\]
Thus \(\Delta_{\mathrm{normal}}=\Delta_{\mathrm{model}}=0\), so all displayed losses are genuinely relative to \(V_{\mathrm{OVS}}\). At \(r=\omega_2=1/2\), the minimum loss over all deterministic feasible loadings, attained by \(b^{\mathrm{const}}\), is \(3/512\), whereas the loss of \(b^{\mathrm{OVS}}\) is \(15/512\).

project_justification.fill: The note proves full published observed-law tangent exhaustion, derives the singular Moore--Penrose canonical projection, gives an attaining fixed-support cross-fitted estimator, and separates aggregate, localized, and published equality equations. It supplies a source-transcribed exact two-period panel-DDD reduction, a complete finite-moment map with pointwise Wald inference for the published-bound comparator gap, and a corrected bounded witness whose best joint constant and componentwise OVS losses are \(3/512\) and \(15/512\), respectively.

prose_updates.related_work: Ortiz--Villavicencio and Sant'Anna provide the identifying architecture, pairwise-score limit theory, constant componentwise benchmark, and, in Supplemental Appendix Lemma A.2, a two-period panel-DDD efficient influence function. Akbari, Kiyavash, and Ghassami's Theorem 5 gives the corresponding nonparametric four-cell panel-DDD efficient influence function. Proposition \(\ref{prop:two-period-eif-reduction}\) maps both formulas term by term to the singleton-comparison specialization of \(\Psi\), including the target-share derivative. The present contribution is the exhaustive global staggered-OVS observed tangent normal, its canonical projection, fixed-support attainment, and pointwise published-gap inference. Chen, Sant'Anna, and Xie derive conditional efficiency for staggered DiD with multiple baselines and comparison cohorts; their observation and restriction system omits the eligibility-gap DDD coordinate, so the papers share a conditional-projection architecture but no nesting is asserted. Newey informs generalized-inverse conditional-moment geometry, and generic DML theory supplies a cross-fitting template; the affine quotient, all-cohort shared-cell calculation, and selected-rank finite-support gap map are proved here.
prose_updates.interpretation: There are three precision frontiers. Conditional loading by \(b^\star(X)\) minimizes variance within the aggregate pairwise-score family. Projection against \(Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\) gives the larger localized model's bound. Projection against the exhaustive \(Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\) gives the published model's canonical gradient and its smallest bound. A loaded pairwise score is therefore called semiparametrically efficient only when its published-normal conditional moment is zero. The corrected witness makes all three normal closures coincide but separates the comparators: conditional weighting beats every deterministic loading by at least \(3/512\) at the benchmark, the best joint constant attains that deterministic minimum, and the componentwise OVS rule loses \(15/512\). The optional \texttt{triplediff} backend can expose the fixed-support efficient target estimator, all three projection diagnostics, and pointwise gap Wald inference when the certified support, rank, overlap, and positivity checks pass.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Population canonicality is pointwise at a conditional-mean interior law and permits singular or redundant published-normal coordinates. Target attainment and gap inference are proved only for fixed finite covariate support. Gap inference assumes positive influence variance and separation from equality by \(\delta_0>0\); it is not uniform across comparator or normal-rank changes. The exact external efficient-influence-function equivalence is confined to the two-period, two-cohort, singleton-comparison panel-DDD specialization. No equivalence or nesting with the distinct staggered-DiD tangent system is claimed. No growing-sieve continuous-covariate remainder or uniform confidence procedure under weak or changing positive eigenvalues of \(K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)\) is proved.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The note covers a fixed finite horizon and target set at conditional-mean interior laws admitting a full-data extension in the global OVS model. It distinguishes the published bound \(V_{\mathrm{OVS}}\), the localized bound \(V_{\mathrm{can}}\), and the aggregate score-family variance \(V_{\mathrm{agg}}\); \(b^\star(X)'\Psi_P\) is not presented as canonical without its published-normal equation. Cross-fitted target inference and comparator-gap inference are pointwise fixed-support results. In the corrected bounded witness, all three normal closures coincide, so \(3/512\) is the minimum published-bound loss over deterministic feasible loadings and \(15/512\) is the componentwise OVS loss at \(r=\omega_2=1/2\). The two-period EIF comparison is an exact special-case reduction only. No continuous-covariate gap Wald theorem, equality-boundary inference, tangent-space nesting with staggered DiD, or rank-uniform guarantee is claimed.
